units.translation: let not fear overcome your mind
for these prophecies father Zeus instilled in Loxias
I shall proclaim to mortals the unerring will of Zeus
⟦1⟧ is also often used by Aeschylus for Apollo, yet always in some relation to his oracles, the ⟦2⟧, Preller-Robert Myth. 286. On ⟦3⟧ in third position (also at 21) to ⟦4⟧.

Verse 20 I have, as Weil earlier, transposed after 26, for which an external indication brought forward by W. lies in the fact that the scholiast on 28 ⟦1⟧ supplements the ⟦2⟧ from 20; with the transmitted order that would be incomprehensible. But also the sequence of thought is considerably improved by the transposition. ⟦3⟧ (to make a proem) stands ⟦4⟧ intransitively, here = ⟦5⟧ transitively. Now according to the transmitted position the invocation of the gods of the oracle would be the proem to the invocation of the other gods; by contrast, after the transposition the entire invocation is the proem to the business of the prophetess, and this is surely the only natural thing. See further below. — In the weak and unclear ⟦6⟧ 21 GHermann correctly found the Aeschylean ⟦7⟧: ⟦8⟧. ⟦9⟧. 252. 591, Frg. 5; thus ⟦10⟧ = ⟦11⟧, namely already as the nearest, and also because of her service to Apollo, 10. 12 ff.
making a prelude I call upon
with good reason she is honored first
justly she is preferred above the rest

⟦1⟧ the same Hermann, since the a is long; thus Ionic (⟦2⟧) ⟦3⟧ (cf. 1, 92). The temple is described by ⟦4⟧, who calls the goddess ⟦5⟧, according to the misunderstanding already found in ⟦6⟧: ⟦7⟧ (scil. ⟦8⟧) ⟦9⟧. The goddess is also mentioned in ⟦10⟧ (according to the tradition likewise as ⟦11⟧), and indeed in Delphic formulae connected with Apollo, Artemis, Leto, whereby the ⟦12⟧ is even better explained. The Delphic inscriptions have ⟦13⟧, Dial.-Inschr. 2503, 12. 2513, 13. 2514, 5. The present indicative denotes the habit of the Pythia, just as ⟦14⟧ and ⟦15⟧ 28f., see there; thus also ⟦16⟧ 22 and ⟦17⟧ 20, while ⟦18⟧ 1 denotes the present prayer.
and by Apollo at Delphi the fairest and greatest temple
I sit down, take my seat
with prayers I make a prelude
with this prayer I give first honor
